content:
Conservative pollster Matt Towery on Monday praised Donald Trump for his tireless efforts in campaigning for GOP candidates across the country ahead of the midterm elections, but couldn’t muster a confident prediction for Republican victories.

Towery joined Fox News to discuss a variety of recent polls he claimed were promising, but only after promoting his new book, stating “the GOP is lucky to have Donald Trump” — and lauding the president for holding rallies in support of his candidates.

“If the Republicans win Kansas, Iowa, Alaska, many of these states, him being there will be the margin of difference of that turnout that will win,” Towery said on “Hannity” Monday. “I’m not going to tell you right now that the Republicans are winning these races.”

“What I’m going to tell you is, they dug themselves out from an incredible hole,” he said to host Sean Hannity. “They were in a big hole, but not the hole The New York Times has. Most of these races now are within the margin of error.”

Towery was referring to a New York Times-Siena University survey released Sunday showing Democratic Senate candidates in all seven swing states leading their Republican opponents. He noted that his polling company, Insider Advantage, shows otherwise.

Towery said his data indicates the Alaska Senate race, between Democratic candidate Mary Peltola and GOP candidate Dan Sullivan, is tied — and has Kansas Republican incumbent Sen. Roger Marshall ahead of Democratic opponent Adam Hamilton by 1 percentage point.

He also said fellow pollster Robert Cahaly of the Trafalgar Group has the Texas race between GOP candidate Ken Paxton and Democratic challenger James Talarico tied, and South Carolina GOP candidate Darline Graham leading Democratic opponent Annie Andrews.

“So this ‘Bad News Bears’ story that we got from The New York Times — now, they could be entirely right,” Towery told Hannity. “And let me just say one thing: You know, these midterms are hard to poll.”

He continued, “And what gives me a pause for concern is, in Georgia, the governor’s race, which is a Republican state, it’s a 50-50 race, according to Insider Advantage tonight. So a lot of work has to be done. The Republicans have to turn out in massive numbers.”

How much of an endorsement those tepid comments actually are remains to be seen. Many analysts have predicted the GOP could lose its majorities in both the House and Senate on Tuesday — after Trump actively decided to make the midterms all about himself amid his disastrous approval ratings.
